correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly identifies the intrinsic parity lattice, derives the 36 facet rays and complete free-sum face taxonomy, classifies all smooth/nonsmooth normal cones, proves each component fan, and derives both transverse toric semigroups. Exact standard-library face checker reproduces (16,88,204,240,144,36,1) and 144+12. It does not extrapolate from finite fields.

evidence: Ohsugi gives a broad Gorenstein criterion for cut polytopes of graphs without K5 minors, including bipartite K2,3 without long induced cycles.
Sakamoto proves h*=(1+t)(1+4t+t²)² for the same intrinsic lattice, but no singular orbit-face stratification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Gorenstein and Hilbert/Ehrhart properties do not imply either the maximal nonsmooth faces or the toric semigroup germs. Known all-graph simplicity criteria imply nonsmoothness but do not imply a full reduced singular support.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: None of these stronger-looking broad theorems entails the precise 144+12 maximal nonsmooth faces and the respective determinantal and triple-Segre local cones. All already-implied normality, smoothness obstruction, degree, and Gorenstein claims are excluded from novelty.

evidence: The 2006 theorem proves globally that cut varieties are smooth iff the graph is C4-minor-free; K2,3 has C4 minors, so it predicts singularity but not its locus.
The 2019 theorem treats simple and simplicial cut polytopes, not a complete singular orbit decomposition.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalent formulations include the normal-fan toric sixfold of the cut polytope and its normal projective cut embedding; both depend on the intrinsic cut-vertex lattice.
